_note: Evidence cards for the Stances page's 'big questions'. Each item points one way: 'pro' or 'con' (labels per card). Roll items: 'yea' says which side a Yea vote is on; her vote, and therefore the item's side, comes from data/votes.json. Release items: 'stmt' must match one release. Headlines are computed in scripts/build_cards.py by the rule stated on each card. Build: python3 -I scripts/build_cards.py (after build_stances.py and build_establishment.py).

items.t: Reintroduced the ICE Security Reform Act (H.R. 673), which would make Homeland Security Investigations an independent agency apart from ICE.
Travelled to El Salvador with three House colleagues to press the administration to return Kilmar Abrego Garcia, wrongfully deported.
Condemned ICE arrests of students Rumeysa Ozturk and Mahmoud Khalil as detentions without due process.
Applauded Long Beach Airport for rejecting Secretary Noem's request to play a video in the terminal; the Oversight Committee opened an investigation.
{Vote} the Laken Riley Act (S. 5). {DemMaj}.
{Vote} the District of Columbia Federal Immigration Compliance Act (H.R. 2056). {DemMaj}.
{Vote} the Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026 (H.R. 7744). {DemMaj}.
{Vote} the Deporting Fraudsters Act (H.R. 1958). {DemMaj}.
{Vote} H.Res. 1128, expressing the House's support for the Department of Homeland Security. {DemMaj}.
{Vote} H.R. 1689, requiring DHS to designate Haiti for temporary protected status. {DemMaj}.

cards.sum: He voted against the enforcement bills below, each time with most Democrats, and for a bill granting Haitians temporary protected status. He has introduced a bill to restructure ICE and has pressed the administration over deportations and arrests.
cards.short: Votes against enforcement bills and for TPS, with most Democrats. Has proposed restructuring ICE and pressed the administration over deportations.

items.t: {Vote} H.Con.Res. 96, expressing support for law enforcement officers. {DemMaj}.
{Vote} the Cashless Bail Reporting Act (H.R. 5625). {DemMaj}.
{Vote} the HALT Fentanyl Act (S. 331). {DemMaj}.
Introduced H.R. 7827, the Stop Militarizing Our Streets Act of 2026.
Announced federal grants for Long Beach law enforcement to enhance transparency and support substance-abuse services.
With the Long Beach city prosecutor, announced a federal grant to improve law-enforcement communication systems.

cards.sum: He voted against the police-support and crime bills below, most with most Democrats, and introduced a bill to curb the militarization of local policing. As mayor and in Congress he has also announced federal grants to Long Beach law enforcement.
cards.short: Voted against the police-support and crime bills below, mostly with Democrats. Has announced federal grants for Long Beach police programs.

items.t: Took {corp26} from {ncorp26} corporate PACs in 2025–26, such as Amazon, Boeing, Google, Meta, UnitedHealth, Walmart and Verizon, plus accounting and law firms such as Deloitte and Akin Gump. In 2023–24 it was {corp24} from {ncorp24}. Counts use each committee's FEC type, then its name.
{Vote} H.J.Res. 25, overturning an IRS rule on gross proceeds reporting by brokers. {DemMaj}.
{Vote} the GENIUS Act (S. 1582), the stablecoin law. {DemMaj}.
{Vote} the CLARITY Act (H.R. 3633), the crypto market-structure bill. {DemMaj}.
{Vote} S.J.Res. 18, overturning the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's overdraft rule. {DemMaj}.
{Vote} S.J.Res. 28, overturning a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule. {DemMaj}.
{Vote} the Faster Labor Contracts Act (H.R. 5408). {DemMaj}.
Cosponsored the Raise the Wage Act of 2025 (H.R. 2743).
Cosponsored the Protecting the Right to Organize Act (H.R. 20), to make it easier to form a union.
Demanded a response from luxury retailer Loro Piana over reports of inequity for Indigenous workers.
Pressed rental car companies on overbooking.

cards.sum: He took {corp26} from {ncorp26} corporate PACs in 2025–26, up from {corp24} in 2023–24, and broke with most Democrats to vote for a crypto-friendly IRS rule rollback and the GENIUS Act. He voted against the CLARITY Act and against overturning two consumer-finance rules, and cosponsors labor and minimum-wage bills.
cards.short: Took {corp26} from corporate PACs in 2025–26, up from {corp24}. Broke with most Democrats on two crypto-related votes, but sided with consumers and labor on others.
